title: SL(C)AMma: Simultaneous Localisation, (Calibration) and Mapping With a Magnetometer Array
comment: 10 pages, 8 figures, 1 table, python implementation available at https://github.com/Tedridge/SL-C-AMma, experimental data available at https://hendeby.gitlab-pages.liu.se/research/magdata/
summary: Indoor localisation techniques suffer from attenuated Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals and from the accumulation of unbounded drift by integration of proprioceptive sensors. Magnetic field-based Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping (SLAM) reduces drift through loop closures by revisiting previously seen locations, but extended exploration of unseen areas remains challenging. Recently, magnetometer arrays have demonstrated significant benefits over single magnetometers, as they can directly estimate the odometry. However, inconsistencies between magnetometer measurements negatively affect odometry estimates and complicate loop closure detection. We propose two filtering algorithms: The first focuses on magnetic field-based SLAM using a magnetometer array (SLAMma). The second extends this to jointly estimate the magnetometer calibration parameters (SLCAMma). We demonstrate, using Monte Carlo simulations, that the calibration parameters can be accurately estimated when there is sufficient orientation excitation, and that magnetometers achieve inter-sensor measurement consistency regardless of the type of motion. Experimental validation on ten datasets confirms these results, and we demonstrate that in cases where single magnetometer SLAM fails, SLAMma and SLCAMma provide good trajectory estimates with, more than 80% drift reduction compared to integration of proprioceptive sensors.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes two filtering algorithms (SLAMma and SLCAMma) for magnetic field-based SLAM with magnetometer arrays that achieve more than 80% drift reduction compared to proprioceptive sensor integration, while accurately estimating magnetometer calibration parameters.
AI.motivation: Indoor localization suffers from GNSS signal attenuation and unbounded drift from integrating proprioceptive sensors. Existing magnetic field-based SLAM reduces drift through loop closures but struggles with extended exploration of unseen areas and sensor inconsistencies.
AI.method: The authors developed two filtering algorithms: (1) SLAMma for magnetic field-based SLAM using a magnetometer array, and (2) SLCAMma which extends SLAMma to jointly estimate magnetometer calibration parameters. They validated these methods using Monte Carlo simulations and experimental validation on ten datasets.
AI.result: Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that calibration parameters can be accurately estimated with sufficient orientation excitation, and magnetometers achieve inter-sensor measurement consistency regardless of motion type. Experimental validation confirms more than 80% drift reduction compared to proprioceptive sensor integration in cases where single magnetometer SLAM fails.
AI.conclusion: The proposed SLAMma and SLCAMma algorithms provide robust trajectory estimation for indoor localization, successfully addressing the limitations of single magnetometer SLAM and significantly reducing drift through magnetometer array-based SLAM with accurate calibration parameter estimation.

title: Radar Odometry Subject to High Tilt Dynamics of Subarctic Environments
summary: Rotating FMCW radar odometry methods often assume flat ground conditions. While this assumption is sufficient in many scenarios, including urban environments or flat mining setups, the highly dynamic terrain of subarctic environments poses a challenge to standard feature extraction and state estimation techniques. This paper benchmarks three existing radar odometry methods under demanding conditions, exhibiting up to 13° in pitch and 4° in roll difference between consecutive scans, with absolute pitch and roll reaching 30° and 8°, respectively. Furthermore, we propose a novel radar-inertial odometry method utilizing tilt-proximity submap search and a hard threshold for vertical displacement between scan points and the estimated axis of rotation. Experimental results demonstrate a state-of-the-art performance of our method on an urban baseline and a 0.3% improvement over the second-best comparative method on a 2-kilometer-long dynamic trajectory. Finally, we analyze the performance of the four evaluated methods on a complex radar sequence characterized by high lateral slip and a steep ditch traversal.

AI.tldr: A novel radar-inertial odometry method using tilt-proximity submap search and vertical displacement thresholding is proposed to address the challenges of rotating FMCW radar odometry in highly dynamic subarctic terrains with large pitch/roll variations.
AI.motivation: Existing rotating FMCW radar odometry methods assume flat ground conditions, which fails in subarctic environments with highly dynamic terrain, causing challenges for standard feature extraction and state estimation techniques.
AI.method: The paper benchmarks three existing radar odometry methods and proposes a novel radar-inertial odometry method utilizing tilt-proximity submap search combined with a hard threshold for vertical displacement between scan points and the estimated axis of rotation.
AI.result: The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on an urban baseline and 0.3% improvement over the second-best method on a 2-kilometer-long dynamic trajectory, successfully handling demanding conditions with up to 13° pitch and 4° roll differences between consecutive scans, and 30° absolute pitch and 8° absolute roll.
AI.conclusion: The novel radar-inertial odometry method effectively addresses the challenges of highly dynamic terrains, demonstrating superior performance on complex radar sequences characterized by high lateral slip and steep ditch traversal.

title: Efficient Reinforcement Learning using Linear Koopman Dynamics for Nonlinear Robotic Systems
summary: This paper presents a model-based reinforcement learning (RL) framework for optimal closed-loop control of nonlinear robotic systems. The proposed approach learns linear lifted dynamics through Koopman operator theory and integrates the resulting model into an actor-critic architecture for policy optimization, where the policy represents a parameterized closed-loop controller. To reduce computational cost and mitigate model rollout errors, policy gradients are estimated using one-step predictions of the learned dynamics rather than multi-step propagation. This leads to an online mini-batch policy gradient framework that enables policy improvement from streamed interaction data. The proposed framework is evaluated on several simulated nonlinear control benchmarks and two real-world hardware platforms, including a Kinova Gen3 robotic arm and a Unitree Go1 quadruped. Experimental results demonstrate improved sample efficiency over model-free RL baselines, superior control performance relative to model-based RL baselines, and control performance comparable to classical model-based methods that rely on exact system dynamics.

AI.tldr: A model-based RL framework using Koopman operator theory to learn linear lifted dynamics for nonlinear robotic control, enabling online mini-batch policy gradient optimization with one-step predictions for improved sample efficiency and computational efficiency.
AI.motivation: The need for optimal closed-loop control of nonlinear robotic systems presents significant challenges, particularly in terms of computational cost and model rollout errors associated with existing model-based reinforcement learning approaches.
AI.method: The approach learns linear lifted dynamics through Koopman operator theory and integrates them into an actor-critic architecture. Policy gradients are estimated using one-step predictions rather than multi-step propagation, enabling an online mini-batch policy gradient framework that operates on streamed interaction data.
AI.result: The framework achieves improved sample efficiency over model-free RL baselines, superior control performance compared to model-based RL baselines, and performance comparable to classical model-based methods that rely on exact system dynamics. Evaluation was conducted on simulated benchmarks and two real-world platforms (Kinova Gen3 robotic arm and Unitree Go1 quadruped).
AI.conclusion: The proposed Koopman operator-based model-based RL framework effectively balances sample efficiency, computational efficiency, and control performance, demonstrating that it can achieve results comparable to classical model-based methods while being more data-efficient than model-free approaches.

title: Strain in Sound: Soft Corrugated Tube for Local Strain Sensing with Acoustic Resonance
comment: 2025 IEEE 8th International Conference on Soft Robotics (RoboSoft). IEEE, 2025
summary: We present a soft corrugated tube sensor designed to estimate strain in each half segment. When air flows through the tube, the internal corrugated cavities induce pressure oscillations that excite the tube's standing wave resonance mode, generating an acoustic tone. Stretching the tube affects both the resonance mode frequency, due to changes in overall length, and the frequency-flow speed relationship, due to variations in cavity width, which is particularly useful for local strain estimation. By sweeping flow rates in a controlled manner, we collected resonance frequency data across flow speeds under various local stretch conditions, enabling a machine learning algorithm (gradient boosting regressor) to estimate segmental strain with high accuracy. The dual-period tube design (3.1 mm and 4.18 mm corrugation periods) achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.8 mm, while the single-period tube (3.1 mm) provided a satisfactory MAE of 1 mm. Testing on a mannequin finger demonstrated the sensor's capability to differentiate multi-joint configurations, showing its potential for estimating non-uniform deformations in soft bodies.

AI.tldr: A soft corrugated tube sensor that uses air flow-induced standing wave resonance to estimate segmental strain, achieving 0.8-1.0 mm accuracy in local strain estimation and demonstrating multi-joint configuration differentiation on a mannequin finger.
AI.motivation: The need to accurately estimate strain in soft bodies, particularly for multi-joint configurations and non-uniform deformations, where conventional strain sensing methods may be inadequate.
AI.method: The sensor exploits air flow through a corrugated tube that creates pressure oscillations exciting standing wave resonance. Stretching affects resonance frequency (via length changes) and frequency-flow speed relationship (via cavity width variations). Data collected by sweeping flow rates under various stretch conditions were used to train a gradient boosting regressor. Two designs were tested: a dual-period tube (3.1mm and 4.18mm corrugation periods) and a single-period tube (3.1mm).
AI.result: The dual-period tube achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.8 mm, while the single-period tube achieved a MAE of 1.0 mm. Testing on a mannequin finger demonstrated the sensor's ability to differentiate multi-joint configurations.
AI.conclusion: The soft corrugated tube sensor shows strong potential for estimating non-uniform deformations in soft bodies and differentiating multi-joint configurations, with promising accuracy for local strain estimation applications.

title: An Efficient Multilevel Preconditioned Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient Method for Incremental Potential Contact
summary: Incremental Potential Contact (IPC) guarantees intersection-free simulation but suffers from high computational costs due to the expensive Hessian assembly and linear solves required by Newton's method. While Preconditioned Nonlinear Conjugate Gradient (PNCG) avoids Hessian assembly, it has historically struggled with poor convergence in stiff, contact-rich scenarios due to the lack of effective preconditioners; simple Jacobi preconditioners fail to capture the global coupling, while advanced hierarchy-based preconditioners like Multilevel Additive Schwarz (MAS) are computationally prohibitive to rebuild at every nonlinear iteration. We present MAS-PNCG, a method that unlocks the power of hierarchical preconditioning for nonlinear optimization. Our key technical innovation is a Sparse-Input Woodbury update algorithm that incrementally adapts the fine-level MAS components to rapidly evolving contact sets. This bypasses the need for full preconditioner rebuilds, reducing maintenance cost to near-zero while capturing the complex spectral properties of the contact system. Furthermore, we replace heuristic PNCG search directions with a Hessian-aware 2D subspace minimization that optimally combines the preconditioned gradient and previous direction. We also apply a fast per-subdomain conservative CCD method that ensures penetration-free trajectories while avoiding overly restrictive global step sizes. Experiments demonstrate that our MAS-PNCG outperforms state-of-the-art Newton-PCG solvers, GIPC and StiffGIPC, both preconditioned with MAS up to 5.66$\times$ and 2.07$\times$ respectively.

AI.tldr: MAS-PNCG combines hierarchical Multilevel Additive Schwarz preconditioning with a Hessian-aware 2D subspace minimization and fast per-subdomain conservative CCD to efficiently solve contact simulations, achieving 5.66× speedup over GIPC and 2.07× over StiffGIPC.
AI.motivation: IPC guarantees intersection-free simulation but has high computational costs due to expensive Hessian assembly and linear solves. PNCG avoids Hessian assembly but struggles with convergence in stiff contact-rich scenarios. Simple Jacobi preconditioners fail to capture global coupling, while advanced hierarchy-based preconditioners like MAS are computationally prohibitive to rebuild at every iteration.
AI.method: 1. Sparse-Input Woodbury update algorithm to incrementally adapt fine-level MAS components to rapidly evolving contact sets, avoiding full preconditioner rebuilds. 2. Replaces heuristic PNCG search directions with Hessian-aware 2D subspace minimization combining preconditioned gradient and previous direction. 3. Fast per-subdomain conservative CCD method for penetration-free trajectories.
AI.result: MAS-PNCG outperforms state-of-the-art Newton-PCG solvers GIPC and StiffGIPC (both preconditioned with MAS) by 5.66× and 2.07× respectively.
AI.conclusion: MAS-PNCG effectively unlocks the power of hierarchical preconditioning for nonlinear optimization in contact simulation, reducing maintenance cost to near-zero while capturing complex spectral properties of contact systems.

title: Soft-Label Governance for Distributional Safety in Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Multi-agent AI systems exhibit emergent risks that no single agent produces in isolation. Existing safety frameworks rely on binary classifications of agent behavior, discarding the uncertainty inherent in proxy-based evaluation. We introduce SWARM (\textbf{S}ystem-\textbf{W}ide \textbf{A}ssessment of \textbf{R}isk in \textbf{M}ulti-agent systems), a simulation framework that replaces binary good/bad labels with \emph{soft probabilistic labels} $p = P(v{=}+1) \in [0,1]$, enabling continuous-valued payoff computation, toxicity measurement, and governance intervention. SWARM implements a modular governance engine with configurable levers (transaction taxes, circuit breakers, reputation decay, and random audits) and quantifies their effects through probabilistic metrics including expected toxicity $\mathbb{E}[1{-}p \mid \text{accepted}]$ and quality gap $\mathbb{E}[p \mid \text{accepted}] - \mathbb{E}[p \mid \text{rejected}]$. Across seven scenarios with five-seed replication, strict governance reduces welfare by over 40\% without improving safety. In parallel, aggressively internalizing system externalities collapses total welfare from a baseline of $+262$ down to $-67$, while toxicity remains invariant. Circuit breakers require careful calibration; overly restrictive thresholds severely diminish system value, whereas an optimal threshold balances moderate welfare with minimized toxicity. Companion experiments show soft metrics detect proxy gaming by self-optimizing agents passing conventional binary evaluations. This basic governance layer applies to live LLM-backed agents (Concordia entities, Claude, GPT-4o Mini) without modification. Results show distributional safety requires \emph{continuous} risk metrics and governance lever calibration involves quantifiable safety-welfare tradeoffs. Source code and project resources are publicly available at https://www.swarm-ai.org/.

AI.tldr: SWARM is a simulation framework that replaces binary agent behavior classifications with soft probabilistic labels p = P(v=+1) ∈ [0,1], enabling continuous-valued payoff computation, toxicity measurement, and governance intervention through configurable levers (transaction taxes, circuit breakers, reputation decay, random audits). The framework quantifies safety-welfare tradeoffs and detects proxy gaming in multi-agent AI systems.
AI.motivation: Multi-agent AI systems exhibit emergent risks that no single agent produces in isolation. Existing safety frameworks rely on binary classifications of agent behavior, which discard the uncertainty inherent in proxy-based evaluation.
AI.method: SWARM implements a modular governance engine with configurable levers (transaction taxes, circuit breakers, reputation decay, random audits) that replaces binary good/bad labels with soft probabilistic labels p = P(v=+1) ∈ [0,1], enabling continuous-valued payoff computation and toxicity measurement. The framework applies to live LLM-backed agents (Concordia entities, Claude, GPT-4o Mini) without modification.
AI.result: Across seven scenarios with five-seed replication: strict governance reduces welfare by over 40% without improving safety; aggressively internalizing system externalities collapses total welfare from +262 to -67 while toxicity remains invariant; circuit breakers require careful calibration - overly restrictive thresholds severely diminish system value, while optimal thresholds balance moderate welfare with minimized toxicity. Soft metrics successfully detect proxy gaming by self-optimizing agents passing conventional binary evaluations.
AI.conclusion: Distributional safety requires continuous risk metrics rather than binary classifications, and governance lever calibration involves quantifiable safety-welfare tradeoffs. This basic governance layer is applicable to live LLM-backed agents without modification.

title: JoyAI-RA 0.1: A Foundation Model for Robotic Autonomy
summary: Robotic autonomy in open-world environments is fundamentally limited by insufficient data diversity and poor cross-embodiment generalization. Existing robotic datasets are often limited in scale and task coverage, while relatively large differences across robot embodiments impede effective behavior knowledge transfer. To address these challenges, we propose JoyAI-RA, a vision-language-action (VLA) embodied foundation model tailored for generalizable robotic manipulation. JoyAI-RA presents a multi-source multi-level pretraining framework that integrates web data, large-scale egocentric human manipulation videos, simulation-generated trajectories, and real-robot data. Through training on heterogeneous multi-source data with explicit action-space unification, JoyAI-RA effectively bridges embodiment gaps, particularly between human manipulation and robotic control, thereby enhancing cross-embodiment behavior learning. JoyAI-RA outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both simulation and real-world benchmarks, especially on diverse tasks with generalization demands.

AI.tldr: JoyAI-RA is a vision-language-action (VLA) embodied foundation model that uses multi-source multi-level pretraining (integrating web data, human manipulation videos, simulation trajectories, and real-robot data) with explicit action-space unification to bridge embodiment gaps and achieve superior cross-embodiment generalization for robotic manipulation tasks.
AI.motivation: Robotic autonomy in open-world environments is limited by insufficient data diversity and poor cross-embodiment generalization. Existing datasets suffer from limited scale and task coverage, while significant differences across robot embodiments impede effective behavior knowledge transfer.
AI.method: A multi-source multi-level pretraining framework that integrates heterogeneous data sources including web data, large-scale egocentric human manipulation videos, simulation-generated trajectories, and real-robot data, with explicit action-space unification to bridge embodiment gaps between human manipulation and robotic control.
AI.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods on both simulation and real-world benchmarks, demonstrating particularly strong performance on diverse tasks with generalization demands.
AI.conclusion: The framework effectively bridges embodiment gaps and enhances cross-embodiment behavior learning, enabling more generalizable robotic manipulation capabilities.

title: Animator-Centric Skeleton Generation on Objects with Fine-Grained Details
summary: Skeleton generation is essential for animating 3D assets, but current deep learning methods remain limited: they cannot handle the growing structural complexity of modern models and offer minimal controllability, creating a major bottleneck for real-world animation workflows. To address this, we propose an animator-centric SG framework that achieves high-quality skeleton prediction on complex inputs while providing intuitive control handles. Our contributions are threefold. First, we curate a large-scale dataset of 82,633 rigged meshes with diverse and complicated structures. Second, we introduce a novel semantic-aware tokenization scheme for auto-regressive modeling. This scheme effectively complements purely geometric prior methods by subdividing bones into semantically meaningful groups, thereby enhancing robustness to structural complexity and enabling a key control mechanism. Third, we design a learnable density interval module that allows animators to exert soft, direct control over bone density. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework not only generates high-quality skeletons for challenging inputs but also successfully fulfills two critical requirements from professional animators.

AI.tldr: An animator-centric framework for high-quality skeleton generation on complex 3D models with semantic-aware tokenization and learnable density control.
AI.motivation: Current deep learning skeleton generation methods are limited by their inability to handle the growing structural complexity of modern 3D models and lack intuitive controllability, creating a major bottleneck for real-world animation workflows.
AI.method: Three key contributions: (1) curated a large-scale dataset of 82,633 rigged meshes with diverse structures; (2) introduced a novel semantic-aware tokenization scheme for auto-regressive modeling that subdivides bones into semantically meaningful groups; (3) designed a learnable density interval module for soft, direct control over bone density.
AI.result: The framework generates high-quality skeletons for challenging inputs and successfully fulfills two critical requirements from professional animators.
AI.conclusion: The proposed animator-centric SG framework overcomes limitations of current methods by achieving robust skeleton prediction on complex inputs while providing intuitive control handles through semantic-aware tokenization and learnable density control.

title: Trust, Lies, and Long Memories: Emergent Social Dynamics and Reputation in Multi-Round Avalon with LLM Agents
summary: We study emergent social dynamics in LLM agents playing The Resistance: Avalon, a hidden-role deception game. Unlike prior work on single-game performance, our agents play repeated games while retaining memory of previous interactions, including who played which roles and how they behaved, enabling us to study how social dynamics evolve. Across 188 games, two key phenomena emerge. First, reputation dynamics emerge organically when agents retain cross-game memory: agents reference past behavior in statements like "I am wary of repeating last game's mistake of over-trusting early success." These reputations are role-conditional: the same agent is described as "straightforward" when playing good but "subtle" when playing evil, and high-reputation players receive 46% more team inclusions. Second, higher reasoning effort supports more strategic deception: evil players more often pass early missions to build trust before sabotaging later ones, 75% in high-effort games vs 36% in low-effort games. Together, these findings show that repeated interaction with memory gives rise to measurable reputation and deception dynamics among LLM agents.

AI.tldr: LLM agents playing repeated rounds of The Resistance: Avalon develop measurable reputation dynamics and strategic deception behaviors when retaining cross-game memory, with high-reputation players receiving more team inclusions and higher reasoning effort enabling more sophisticated deception tactics.
AI.motivation: Prior research focused on single-game performance; this study examines how social dynamics evolve when agents play repeated games while retaining memory of previous interactions and behaviors.
AI.method: LLM agents played 188 rounds of The Resistance: Avalon (a hidden-role deception game) with memory of previous games, including role assignments and behavioral patterns, allowing observation of evolving social dynamics.
AI.result: Two key phenomena emerged: (1) Reputation dynamics organically developed, with agents referencing past behavior and role-conditional reputations (same agent described as "straightforward" when good but "subtle" when evil), and high-reputation players received 46% more team inclusions; (2) Higher reasoning effort enabled more strategic deception - evil players passed early missions to build trust before sabotaging (75% in high-effort vs 36% in low-effort games).
AI.conclusion: Repeated interaction with memory gives rise to measurable reputation and deception dynamics among LLM agents, demonstrating that social behaviors can emerge organically from LLM interactions in multi-game settings.

title: Toward Safe Autonomous Robotic Endovascular Interventions using World Models
comment: This manuscript is a preprint and has been submitted to the IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) 2026
summary: Autonomous mechanical thrombectomy (MT) presents substantial challenges due to highly variable vascular geometries and the requirements for accurate, real-time control. While reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for the automation of endovascular navigation, existing approaches often show limited robustness when faced with diverse patient anatomies or extended navigation horizons. In this work, we investigate a world-model-based framework for autonomous endovascular navigation built on TD-MPC2, a model-based RL method that integrates planning and learned dynamics. We evaluate a TD-MPC2 agent trained on multiple navigation tasks across hold out patient-specific vasculatures and benchmark its performance against the state-of-the-art Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm agent. Both approaches are further validated in vitro using patient-specific vascular phantoms under fluoroscopic guidance. In simulation, TD-MPC2 demonstrates a significantly higher mean success rate than SAC (58% vs. 36%, p < 0.001), and mean tip contact forces of 0.15 N, well below the proposed 1.5 N vessel rupture threshold. Mean success rates for TD-MPC2 (68%) were comparable to SAC (60%) in vitro, but TD-MPC2 achieved superior path ratios (p = 0.017) at the cost of longer procedure times (p < 0.001). Together, these results provide the first demonstration of autonomous MT navigation validated across both hold out in silico data and fluoroscopy-guided in vitro experiments, highlighting the promise of world models for safe and generalizable AI-assisted endovascular interventions.

title: Anchor-and-Resume Concession Under Dynamic Pricing for LLM-Augmented Freight Negotiation
summary:
Freight brokerages negotiate thousands of carrier rates daily under dynamic pricing conditions where models frequently revise targets mid-conversation. Classical time-dependent concession frameworks use a fixed shape parameter $β$ that cannot adapt to these updates. Deriving $β$ from the live spread enables adaptation but introduces a new problem: a pricing shift can cause the formula to retract a previous offer, violating monotonicity. LLM-powered brokers offer flexibility but require expensive reasoning models, produce non-deterministic pricing, and remain vulnerable to prompt injection.
  We propose a two-index anchor-and-resume framework that addresses both limitations. A spread-derived $β$ maps each load's margin structure to the correct concession posture, while the anchor-and-resume mechanism guarantees monotonically non-decreasing offers under arbitrary pricing shifts. All pricing decisions remain in a deterministic formula; the LLM, when used, serves only as a natural-language translation layer. Empirical evaluation across 115,125 negotiations shows that the adaptive $β$ tailors behavior by regime: in narrow spreads, it concedes quickly to prioritize deal closure and load coverage; in medium and wide spreads, it matches or exceeds the best fixed-$β$ baselines in broker savings. Against an unconstrained 20-billion-parameter LLM broker, it achieves similar agreement rates and savings. Against LLM-powered carriers as more realistic stochastic counterparties, it maintains comparable savings and higher agreement rates than against rule-based opponents. By decoupling the LLM from pricing logic, the framework scales horizontally to thousands of concurrent negotiations with negligible inference cost and transparent decision-making.

AI.tldr: A two-index anchor-and-resume framework that adapts concession parameters dynamically via spread-derived β while maintaining monotonic pricing decisions, using LLM only as a translation layer for natural-language interface.
AI.motivation: Freight brokerages face dynamic pricing with frequent mid-conversation updates. Classical time-dependent concession frameworks use fixed β parameters that cannot adapt, while LLM-powered brokers suffer from high costs, non-deterministic pricing, and prompt injection vulnerabilities.
AI.method: Proposes a two-index framework combining: 1) a spread-derived β parameter that adapts to live market conditions, and 2) an anchor-and-resume mechanism that guarantees monotonically non-decreasing offers under arbitrary pricing shifts. The LLM is used only as a natural-language translation layer for the user interface, keeping all pricing decisions in deterministic formulas.
AI.result: Evaluated across 115,125 negotiations. The adaptive β tailors behavior by regime: concedes quickly in narrow spreads to prioritize deal closure and load coverage, while matching or exceeding best fixed-β baselines in medium and wide spreads. Against a 20B-parameter LLM broker, achieves similar agreement rates and savings. Against LLM-powered carriers, maintains comparable savings with higher agreement rates than against rule-based opponents.
AI.conclusion: By decoupling the LLM from pricing logic, the framework scales horizontally to thousands of concurrent negotiations with negligible inference cost and transparent decision-making, addressing the limitations of both classical approaches and pure LLM solutions.

title: LLM-Guided Safety Agent for Edge Robotics with an ISO-Compliant Perception-Compute-Control Architecture
summary: Ensuring functional safety in human-robot interaction is challenging because AI perception is inherently probabilistic, whereas industrial standards require deterministic behavior. We present an LLM-guided safety agent for edge robotics, built on an ISO-compliant low-latency perception-compute-control architecture. Our method translates natural-language safety regulations into executable predicates and deploys them through a redundant heterogeneous edge runtime. For fault-tolerant closed-loop execution under edge constraints, we adopt a symmetric dual-modular redundancy design with parallel independent execution for low-latency perception, computation, and control. We prototype the system on a dual-RK3588 platform and evaluate it in representative human-robot interaction scenarios. The results demonstrate a practical edge implementation path toward ISO 13849 Category 3 and PL d using cost-effective hardware, supporting practical deployment of safety-critical embodied AI.

AI.tldr: An LLM-guided safety agent for edge robotics that translates natural-language safety regulations into executable predicates, using a dual-modular redundancy design to achieve ISO-compliant safety levels on cost-effective hardware.
AI.motivation: Functional safety in human-robot interaction is challenging because AI perception is inherently probabilistic, whereas industrial standards require deterministic behavior. There is a need for practical edge implementation paths for safety-critical embodied AI systems that can meet strict safety requirements.
AI.method: Built on an ISO-compliant low-latency perception-compute-control architecture; uses LLM to translate natural-language safety regulations into executable predicates deployed through redundant heterogeneous edge runtime; adopts symmetric dual-modular redundancy design with parallel independent execution; prototyped on dual-RK3588 platform.
AI.result: Demonstrates a practical edge implementation path toward ISO 13849 Category 3 and PL d safety levels using cost-effective hardware in representative human-robot interaction scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Supports practical deployment of safety-critical embodied AI systems with affordable hardware, bridging the gap between probabilistic AI perception and deterministic industrial safety requirements.

title: Bimanual Robot Manipulation via Multi-Agent In-Context Learning
summary: Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as powerful reasoning engines for embodied control. In particular, In-Context Learning (ICL) enables off-the-shelf, text-only LLMs to predict robot actions without any task-specific training while preserving their generalization capabilities. Applying ICL to bimanual manipulation remains challenging, as the high-dimensional joint action space and tight inter-arm coordination constraints rapidly overwhelm standard context windows. To address this, we introduce BiCICLe (Bimanual Coordinated In-Context Learning), the first framework that enables standard LLMs to perform few-shot bimanual manipulation without fine-tuning. BiCICLe frames bimanual control as a multi-agent leader-follower problem, decoupling the action space into sequential, conditioned single-arm predictions. This naturally extends to Arms' Debate, an iterative refinement process, and to the introduction of a third LLM-as-Judge to evaluate and select the most plausible coordinated trajectories. Evaluated on 13 tasks from the TWIN benchmark, BiCICLe achieves up to 71.1% average success rate, outperforming the best training-free baseline by 6.7 percentage points and surpassing most supervised methods. We further demonstrate strong few-shot generalization on novel tasks.

AI.tldr: BiCICLe is a framework for few-shot bimanual manipulation using In-Context Learning with large language models. It frames bimanual control as a leader-follower problem with an iterative Arms' Debate process and an LLM-as-Judge for trajectory selection, achieving 71.1% success rate on 13 TWIN benchmark tasks.
AI.motivation: Standard LLMs can perform embodied control via In-Context Learning, but bimanual manipulation remains challenging due to high-dimensional joint action spaces and tight inter-arm coordination constraints that overwhelm standard context windows.
AI.method: BiCICLe frames bimanual control as a multi-agent leader-follower problem, decoupling the action space into sequential single-arm predictions. It introduces "Arms' Debate" (iterative refinement) and an "LLM-as-Judge" that evaluates and selects the most plausible coordinated trajectories.
AI.result: BiCICLe achieves up to 71.1% average success rate on 13 tasks from the TWIN benchmark, outperforming the best training-free baseline by 6.7 percentage points and surpassing most supervised methods.
AI.conclusion: BiCICLe demonstrates strong few-shot generalization on novel tasks, establishing the first framework for standard LLMs to perform few-shot bimanual manipulation without fine-tuning.

title: Stochastic Barrier Certificates in the Presence of Dynamic Obstacles
summary: Safety of stochastic dynamic systems in environments with dynamic obstacles is studied in this paper through the lens of stochastic barrier functions. We introduce both time-invariant and time-varying barrier certificates for discrete-time, continuous-space systems subject to uncertainty, which provide certified lower bounds on the probability of remaining within a safe set over a finite horizon. These certificates explicitly account for time-varying unsafe regions induced by obstacle dynamics. By leveraging Bellman's optimality perspective, the time-varying formulation directly captures temporal structure and yields less conservative bounds than state-of-the-art approaches. By restricting certificates to polynomial functions, we show that time-varying barrier synthesis can be formulated as a convex sum-of-squares program, enabling tractable optimization. Empirical evaluations on nonlinear systems with dynamic obstacles show that time-varying certificates consistently achieve tight guarantees, demonstrating improved accuracy and scalability over state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces time-invariant and time-varying stochastic barrier certificates for discrete-time continuous-space systems with dynamic obstacles, providing certified lower bounds on safety probability. By leveraging Bellman's optimality perspective and restricting certificates to polynomial functions, the synthesis is formulated as a convex sum-of-squares program, achieving tighter guarantees and improved scalability over state-of-the-art methods.
AI.motivation: Safety certification for stochastic dynamic systems in environments with dynamic obstacles is challenging, requiring certified lower bounds on the probability of remaining within a safe set while accounting for time-varying unsafe regions induced by obstacle dynamics. Existing approaches often yield conservative bounds.
AI.method: The authors introduce both time-invariant and time-varying barrier certificates for discrete-time, continuous-space stochastic systems. By leveraging Bellman's optimality perspective, the time-varying formulation captures temporal structure. Restricting certificates to polynomial functions allows formulation of the barrier synthesis as a convex sum-of-squares program, enabling tractable optimization.
AI.result: Empirical evaluations on nonlinear systems with dynamic obstacles demonstrate that time-varying certificates consistently achieve tight guarantees, with improved accuracy and scalability compared to state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: The time-varying formulation provides less conservative bounds than state-of-the-art approaches, while the polynomial restriction makes the synthesis tractable. This demonstrates that time-varying barrier certificates can effectively certify safety for stochastic systems with dynamic obstacles.

title: Toward Cooperative Driving in Mixed Traffic: An Adaptive Potential Game-Based Approach with Field Test Verification
summary: Connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs), which represent a significant advancement in autonomous driving technology, have the potential to greatly increase traffic safety and efficiency through cooperative decision-making. However, existing methods often overlook the individual needs and heterogeneity of cooperative participants, making it difficult to transfer them to environments where they coexist with human-driven vehicles (HDVs).To address this challenge, this paper proposes an adaptive potential game (APG) cooperative driving framework. First, the system utility function is established on the basis of a general form of individual utility and its monotonic relationship, allowing for the simultaneous optimization of both individual and system objectives. Second, the Shapley value is introduced to compute each vehicle's marginal utility within the system, allowing its varying impact to be quantified. Finally, the HDV preference estimation is dynamically refined by continuously comparing the observed HDV behavior with the APG's estimated actions, leading to improvements in overall system safety and efficiency. Ablation studies demonstrate that adaptively updating Shapley values and HDV preference estimation significantly improve cooperation success rates in mixed traffic. Comparative experiments further highlight the APG's advantages in terms of safety and efficiency over other cooperative methods. Moreover, the applicability of the approach to real-world scenarios was validated through field tests.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an adaptive potential game (APG) cooperative driving framework that addresses the heterogeneity of cooperative participants in mixed traffic by introducing Shapley value-based marginal utility computation and dynamic HDV preference estimation, demonstrating improved safety and efficiency in both simulation and field tests compared to existing methods.
AI.motivation: Existing cooperative driving methods overlook individual needs and heterogeneity of participants, making them difficult to transfer to environments coexisting with human-driven vehicles (HDVs). The paper aims to address this challenge by developing a framework that simultaneously optimizes individual and system objectives while accounting for heterogeneous participants.
AI.method: The APG framework consists of three main components: (1) a system utility function based on individual utility with monotonic relationship to simultaneously optimize individual and system objectives; (2) Shapley value calculation to quantify each vehicle's marginal utility within the system; (3) dynamic HDV preference estimation refined by continuously comparing observed HDV behavior with APG's estimated actions.
AI.result: Ablation studies demonstrate that adaptively updating Shapley values and HDV preference estimation significantly improve cooperation success rates in mixed traffic. Comparative experiments show APG's advantages in safety and efficiency over other cooperative methods. Field tests validate the approach's applicability to real-world scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The adaptive potential game framework effectively addresses the heterogeneity challenge in mixed traffic environments, successfully balancing individual and system objectives while improving overall traffic safety and efficiency, as confirmed through both simulation experiments and field validation.

title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment
summary: Industrial robotic manipulation demands reliable long-horizon execution across embodiments, tasks, and changing object distributions. While Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong generalization, they remain fundamentally reactive. By optimizing the next action given the current observation without evaluating potential futures, they are brittle to the compounding failure modes of long-horizon tasks. Cortex 2.0 shifts from reactive control to plan-and-act by generating candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, scoring them for expected success and efficiency, then committing only to the highest-scoring candidate. We evaluate Cortex 2.0 on a single-arm and dual-arm manipulation platform across four tasks of increasing complexity: pick and place, item and trash sorting, screw sorting, and shoebox unpacking. Cortex 2.0 consistently outperforms state-of-the-art Vision-Language-Action baselines, achieving the best results across all tasks. The system remains reliable in unstructured environments characterized by heavy clutter, frequent occlusions, and contact-rich manipulation, where reactive policies fail. These results demonstrate that world-model-based planning can operate reliably in complex industrial environments.

AI.tldr: Cortex 2.0 shifts from reactive to plan-and-act control by generating and scoring candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, achieving superior performance in complex industrial robotic manipulation tasks across single-arm and dual-arm platforms.
AI.motivation: Industrial robotic manipulation requires reliable long-horizon execution across embodiments, tasks, and changing object distributions. While Vision-Language-Action models generalize well, they are fundamentally reactive and brittle to compounding failure modes in long-horizon tasks.
AI.method: Cortex 2.0 generates candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, scores them for expected success and efficiency, and commits only to the highest-scoring candidate, representing a shift from reactive control to plan-and-act control.
AI.result: Cortex 2.0 consistently outperforms state-of-the-art Vision-Language-Action baselines across all tasks (pick and place, item and trash sorting, screw sorting, shoebox unpacking) on both single-arm and dual-arm platforms, remaining reliable in unstructured environments with heavy clutter, frequent occlusions, and contact-rich manipulation.
AI.conclusion: World-model-based planning can operate reliably in complex industrial environments, demonstrating that plan-and-act approaches are more suitable for long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks than reactive policies.

title: Onboard Wind Estimation for Small UAVs Equipped with Low-Cost Sensors: An Aerodynamic Model-Integrated Filtering Approach
summary: To enable autonomous wind estimation for energy-efficient flight in small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), this study proposes a method that estimates flight states and wind using only the low-cost essential onboard sensors required for autonomous flight, without relying on additional wind measurement devices. The core of the method includes an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) integrated with the aerodynamic model and an Adaptive Moving Average Estimation (AMAE) technique, which improves the accuracy and smoothness of the wind estimation. Simulation results show that the approach efficiently estimates both steady and time-varying 3D wind vectors without requiring flow angle measurements. The impact of aerodynamic model accuracy on wind estimation errors is also analyzed to assess practical applicability. Flight tests validate the effectiveness of the method and its feasibility for real-time onboard computation. Additionally, uncertainties and error sources encountered during testing are systematically examined, providing a foundation for further refinement.

AI.tldr: A low-cost onboard method for autonomous 3D wind estimation in small UAVs using EKF integrated with aerodynamic model and Adaptive Moving Average Estimation (AMAE) technique, validated through simulation and flight tests.
AI.motivation: To enable energy-efficient autonomous flight in small UAVs by estimating wind states without relying on additional wind measurement devices or expensive sensors.
AI.method: Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) integrated with an aerodynamic model and Adaptive Moving Average Estimation (AMAE) technique, using only onboard sensors required for autonomous flight.
AI.result: Simulation results demonstrate efficient estimation of both steady and time-varying 3D wind vectors without flow angle measurements; flight tests validate the method's effectiveness and feasibility for real-time onboard computation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method is effective for wind estimation, feasible for real-time onboard computation, and provides a foundation for further refinement by systematically analyzing uncertainties and error sources encountered during testing.

title: ETac: A Lightweight and Efficient Tactile Simulation Framework for Learning Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Tactile sensors are increasingly integrated into dexterous robotic manipulators to enhance contact perception. However, learning manipulation policies that rely on tactile sensing remains challenging, primarily due to the trade-off between fidelity and computational cost of soft-body simulations. To address this, we present ETac, a tactile simulation framework that models elastomeric soft-body interactions with both high fidelity and efficiency. ETac employs a lightweight data-driven deformation propagation model to capture soft-body contact dynamics, achieving high simulation quality and boosting efficiency that enables large-scale policy training. When serving as the simulation backend, ETac produces surface deformation estimates comparable to FEM and demonstrates applicability for modeling real tactile sensors. Then, we showcase its capability in training a blind grasping policy that leverages large-area tactile feedback to manipulate diverse objects. Running on a single RTX 4090 GPU, ETac supports reinforcement learning across 4,096 parallel environments, achieving a total throughput of 869 FPS. The resulting policy reaches an average success rate of 84.45% across four object types, underscoring ETac's potential to make tactile-based skill learning both efficient and scalable.

AI.tldr: ETac is a high-fidelity yet efficient tactile simulation framework for robotic manipulators that uses a lightweight data-driven deformation propagation model to enable large-scale reinforcement learning of tactile-based grasping policies.
AI.motivation: Learning manipulation policies that rely on tactile sensing is challenging due to the trade-off between fidelity and computational cost in soft-body simulations, which limits large-scale policy training.
AI.method: ETac employs a lightweight data-driven deformation propagation model to capture soft-body contact dynamics, achieving both high simulation quality and efficiency. It supports reinforcement learning across 4,096 parallel environments with 869 FPS throughput on a single RTX 4090 GPU.
AI.result: ETac produces surface deformation estimates comparable to FEM and demonstrates applicability for modeling real tactile sensors. The resulting blind grasping policy achieves an average success rate of 84.45% across four object types.
AI.conclusion: ETac enables efficient and scalable tactile-based skill learning, demonstrating that high-fidelity tactile simulation combined with computational efficiency can significantly improve manipulation policy training performance.

title: AdaTracker: Learning Adaptive In-Context Policy for Cross-Embodiment Active Visual Tracking
summary: Realizing active visual tracking with a single unified model across diverse robots is challenging, as the physical constraints and motion dynamics vary drastically from one platform to another. Existing approaches typically train separate models for each embodiment, leading to poor scalability and limited generalization. To address this, we propose AdaTracker, an adaptive in-context policy learning framework that robustly tracks targets on diverse robot morphologies. Our key insight is to explicitly model embodiment-specific constraints through an Embodiment Context Encoder, which infers embodiment-specific constraints from history. This contextual representation dynamically modulates a Context-Aware Policy, enabling it to infer optimal control actions for unseen embodiments in a zero-shot manner. To enhance robustness, we introduce two auxiliary objectives to ensure accurate context identification and temporal consistency. Experiments in both simulation and the real world demonstrate that AdaTracker significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in cross-embodiment generalization, sample efficiency, and zero-shot adaptation.

AI.tldr: AdaTracker is an adaptive in-context policy learning framework for cross-embodiment active visual tracking, using an Embodiment Context Encoder to infer embodiment-specific constraints that modulate a Context-Aware Policy, achieving superior generalization, sample efficiency, and zero-shot adaptation compared to state-of-the-art methods.
AI.motivation: Active visual tracking across diverse robots is challenging due to varying physical constraints and motion dynamics; existing separate-model approaches suffer from poor scalability and limited generalization, necessitating a unified framework that can adapt to different robot morphologies.
AI.method: AdaTracker employs an Embodiment Context Encoder that infers embodiment-specific constraints from history, which dynamically modulates a Context-Aware Policy to infer optimal control actions. The framework includes two auxiliary objectives for accurate context identification and temporal consistency.
AI.result: AdaTracker significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in cross-embodiment generalization, sample efficiency, and zero-shot adaptation, demonstrated through both simulation and real-world experiments.
AI.conclusion: The proposed adaptive in-context policy learning framework successfully addresses the challenge of cross-embodiment visual tracking, enabling robust performance across diverse robot morphologies without requiring per-embodiment training.

title: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Adaptive Ultrasound-Guided Needle Insertion and Needle Tracking
summary: Ultrasound (US)-guided needle insertion is a critical yet challenging procedure due to dynamic imaging conditions and difficulties in needle visualization. Many methods have been proposed for automated needle insertion, but they often rely on hand-crafted pipelines with modular controllers, whose performance degrades in challenging cases. In this paper, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model is proposed for adaptive and automated US-guided needle insertion and tracking on a robotic ultrasound (RUS) system. This framework provides a unified approach to needle tracking and needle insertion control, enabling real-time, dynamically adaptive adjustment of insertion based on the obtained needle position and environment awareness. To achieve real-time and end-to-end tracking, a Cross-Depth Fusion (CDF) tracking head is proposed, integrating shallow positional and deep semantic features from the large-scale vision backbone. To adapt the pretrained vision backbone for tracking tasks, a Tracking-Conditioning (TraCon) register is introduced for parameter-efficient feature conditioning. After needle tracking, an uncertainty-aware control policy and an asynchronous VLA pipeline are presented for adaptive needle insertion control, ensuring timely decision-making for improved safety and outcomes. Extensive experiments on both needle tracking and insertion show that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art trackers and manual operation, achieving higher tracking accuracy, improved insertion success rates, and reduced procedure time, highlighting promising directions for RUS-based intelligent intervention.

AI.tldr: A Vision-Language-Action model for real-time, adaptive US-guided needle insertion and tracking on robotic ultrasound, using Cross-Depth Fusion tracking and uncertainty-aware control.
AI.motivation: Ultrasound-guided needle insertion is challenging due to dynamic imaging conditions and needle visualization difficulties. Existing methods rely on hand-crafted pipelines with modular controllers that degrade performance in challenging cases.
AI.method: A unified VLA framework with Cross-Depth Fusion (CDF) tracking head (integrates shallow positional and deep semantic features) and Tracking-Conditioning (TraCon) register for parameter-efficient feature conditioning. An uncertainty-aware control policy and asynchronous VLA pipeline enable adaptive needle insertion control.
AI.result: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art trackers and manual operation, achieving higher tracking accuracy, improved insertion success rates, and reduced procedure time.
AI.conclusion: The method demonstrates promising directions for robotic ultrasound-based intelligent intervention, providing real-time, dynamically adaptive needle tracking and control.

title: Benefits of Low-Cost Bio-Inspiration in the Age of Overparametrization
summary: While Central Pattern Generators (CPGs) and Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP) are widely used paradigms in robot control, few systematic studies have been performed on the relative merits of large parameter spaces. In contexts where input and output spaces are small and performance is bounded, having more parameters to optimize may actively hinder the learning process instead of empowering it. To empirically measure this, we submit a given robot morphology, with limited proprioceptive capabilities, to controller optimization under two bio-inspired paradigms (CPGs and MLPs) with evolutionary- and reinforcement- trainer protocols. By varying parameter spaces across multiple reward functions, we observe that shallow MLPs and densely connected CPGs result in better performance when compared to deeper MLPs or Actor-Critic architectures. To account for the relationship between said performance and the number of parameters, we introduce a Parameter Impact metric which demonstrates that the additional parameters required by the reinforcement technique do not translate into better performance, thus favouring evolutionary strategies.
